answer: A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, as every participant consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. The karst cap is applied at intake and summit shows the per-origin counts. At most 3 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a vertex tag. That is 17 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
